//: Type checking for a plain-JavaScript project, with no build step and nothing added
to the repo. `npm run typecheck` (in backend/) runs it; CI runs it too. See
REFERENCE.md section 39 for the full rationale.
WHY jsconfig.json AND NOT tsconfig.json: they are the same file to the compiler,
but the name is a signal. jsconfig means 'this is a JavaScript project' — VS Code
and other editors pick it up automatically, so a newcomer who opens this repo gets
hover documentation and inline type errors with no setup at all. That editor
experience is most of the point; the CI job is the part that keeps it honest.
WHY checkJs IS FALSE: adoption is per file, via a `// @ts-check` comment at the
top. Turning it on globally would report thousands of errors across db.js and
server.js on day one, which is the same as reporting none — nobody reads a wall of
output. A file opts in when it has been made clean, and once opted in it stays
clean because CI fails otherwise. Adding `// @ts-check` to a file is the whole
adoption step.
WHY strict IS FALSE, with strictNullChecks called out separately: strictNullChecks
against this codebase reports ~600 'possibly undefined' findings in db.js alone.
Most are places where the code is genuinely correct because a query cannot return
no rows, and proving that to the compiler means annotating far more than it would
catch. That is a real future improvement, not a first step — see section 39.
There is NO node_modules here and there never will be. @types/node is installed
globally (like Playwright) and found via typeRoots, so nothing is added to the repo
and `npm install` stays unnecessary.
